title: Quirky field repair & ops notes (micro-protocols)
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratch for micro-protocols to repair weird fields during annotation triage. These are small, pragmatic heuristics to run in a lightweight pre-clean pipeline or as annotator hints. Not final — tests needed, but I wanted a consolidated place for oddities we keep re-encountering in user-content datasets.

Principles (summary):
- Prefer non-destructive fixes: add a "repaired_value" field when possible instead of overwriting original.
- Keep heuristics conservative: high precision > recall for automatic fixes; lower-confidence suggestions should be flagged for human review.
- Record provenance: which rule triggered, regex/id, and sample score.

Micro-protocols and examples (rule, rationale, example):

1) Phone-field salvage (rule: detect, normalize, preserve ext)
- Trigger: field contains digits + separators and either 'ext', 'x', '#', or parentheses with >3 digits.
- Normalize to E.164 when country context known; otherwise store as "national-ish" format and extract extension separately.
- If contains emoji or text noise ("☎️+1-555-..."), strip non-numeric glyphs except leading + and commas used for pauses.

Examples:
- Original: "(415) 555-1212 x123"
  Repaired: "+1-415-555-1212"; extension: "123"; rule: phone-ext-v1
- Original: "☎️ 0207 555 6666"
  Repaired: "+44-20-7555-6666" (only when region=UK in metadata); otherwise "0207 555 6666" and flagged for review
- Original: "+1 (800) HELP-ME"
  Repaired: "+1-800-435-7633" (back-transliterate letters when obvious) OR flag if ambiguous; rule allowed only for top-level vanity numbers

2) Address fragments / crumbs (rule: detect URL-encoded, emoji-delimited, or concatenated fragments)
- Detect if address field contains uncommon separators like "|", "::", "🔥" or sequences of tokens that look like street+city with missing commas. Try heuristic split by staple tokens (st, ave, blvd, rd, city names list).
- If the string contains HTML entities (&, <), unescape but do NOT attempt to guess missing parts. Tag as "unescaped-html".

Examples:
- Original: "123 Main St🔥Springfield MA"
  Repaired suggestion: "123 Main St, Springfield, MA"; rule: join-on-unicode-sep-v0
- Original: "29th floor & suite 290"
  Repaired: unescape to "29th floor & suite 290"; flag for building-number normalization if separate field exists

3) SKU vs internal-id ambiguity (rule: identification by token morphology)
- If field contains mixed-case with hyphens and lengths in the 6–20 char range, and dataset has both SKU and user-id fields, prefer marking as SKU when alpha segments present.
- Add hint: if downstream model treats hyphenated tokens as single token, consider splitting on hyphen for embedding/lookup.

Example:
- Original: "ABC-123-xyz"
  Action: annotate as sku_candidate=true, suggest split variants ["ABC", "123", "xyz"]

4) HTML / escaped snippets (rule: detect <tags>, <, >, %3C patterns)
- If >3 angle-bracket tokens or common HTML entities present, tag as "html-snippet".
- Try to remove tags if field should be plain text, but store raw snapshot for audit. For small inline tags (like <b>), prefer strip_tags. For scripts or iframes, flag for security review.

5) Multilingual tokens jammed (rule: script detection + whitespace heuristics)
- If field mixes scripts (Latin + Cyrillic + Han) and length < 120, attempt to split by script boundaries and provide language-suggested repairs.
- Avoid auto-merge where scripts alternate frequently; send to human.

Examples:
- Original: "John Иван 李"
  Suggest split: ["John", "Иван", "李"]; assign separate name components if possible

6) Trailing control-chars, zero-width or invisible (rule: unicode category scan)
- Strip U+200B..U+200F and other zero-width markers unless used intentionally (rare). If stripped, record original and mark as repaired_invisible_chars

Edge heuristics / short regex snippets to try (for implementation):
- phone-ext-v1: /(?i)(?:\+?\d[\d\-\s().]{6,}\s*(?:ext|x|#)\s*\d{1,6})/
- vanity-phone-detect: /[A-Za-z]{3,}-\d{1,4}/ (guarded)
- unescaped-html: /&(?:amp|lt|gt|quot|#x?[0-9a-fA-F]+);/
- invisible-probe: /[\u200B-\u200F\uFEFF]/

Decision rubric for auto-fix vs review (short):
- Auto-fix allowed if: high-confidence pattern match (precision > 98% in our small eval), transformation lossless or reversible (we keep original), and domain metadata matches (country, field schema).
- Suggest-only if: multiple plausible fixes, cross-field inconsistency, or low confidence.
- Block/flag if: fix touches PII classification (SSN-like numbers), or content might be user-provided HTML/scripts.

Quick annotation hints for labelers (to paste into task UI):
- "If phone contains 'x' or 'ext', extract extension into metadata; keep original untouched."
- "Prefer leaving poorly-formed multilingual names for human adjudication — splitting by script is a suggestion only."
- "When you see 'Suite' or 'FL', prefer 'suite' normalization only if street number and city fields present."

Small test sample (hand-crafted, put in triage queue):
- id: sample-0211 | field: contact | raw: "(800) 555-9999 ext 5" | expect: phone:+1-800-555-9999 ; ext:5 ; rule: phone-ext-v1
- id: sample-0212 | field: address | raw: "45B Baker St::London" | expect: "45B Baker St, London" ; rule: join-on-unicode-sep-v0
- id: sample-0213 | field: misc | raw: "user=abc-123-XYZ" | expect: mark sku_candidate=true
- id: sample-0214 | field: bio | raw: "I love coding & coffee <script>alert(1)</script>" | expect: tag html-snippet; strip safe tags and flag scripts

Open questions / things to test:
- How aggressive should vanity-number back-transliteration be? We need a small recall test against a labelled vanity-phone set. (PR: github PR 84 includes a tiny set)
- Should SKU heuristics be a separate micro-service or a fast regex pass in the client? Latency vs accuracy tradeoff.
- How to present "repaired_value" to downstream models so they don't double-learn cleaned format? Propose: include both original_text and repaired_text as separate tokens in embed pipeline.

Immediate TODOs (for next week):
- Run evaluation harness for phone-ext-v1 on 1k random phone samples — target precision > 98% before enabling auto-fix. Assigned: Noah.
- Add "invisible-char" detector to pre-clean step; log counts by dataset. Assigned: me (Priya).
- Create a tiny conll-style sample bundle for address-join cases and push to JIRA-DF-981. Assigned: Lena.

Notes to self: keep rules small and auditable; store example-trigger logs so we can rollback easy. If this doc proliferates, we should move a cleaned subset to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/labeling-heuristics later.

-- Priya
(really quick personal scratch; will flesh into a shared runbook if experiments look good)
